## Structure and components

- [statement] The Mouton-Liger review describes proteasomal and lysosomal pathways that degrade damaged mitochondrial components outside mitochondria. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In dopaminergic neurons derived from patients with idiopathic and familial Parkinson’s disease, Burbulla and colleagues report a cascade linking mitochondrial oxidant stress through oxidized dopamine accumulation to reduced glucocerebrosidase activity and lysosomal dysfunction. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6021018/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] Burbulla and colleagues report that the toxic cascade was observed in human but not mouse Parkinson’s disease neurons, partly because of species-specific dopamine metabolism. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6021018/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] Wang and Xu propose that upstream PINK1/Parkin activation can become partly uncoupled from downstream mitochondrial clearance under Parkinson’s disease-relevant conditions; pathway activation therefore does not necessarily demonstrate completed mitophagy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-24) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13341507/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] The Mouton-Liger review describes excessive microglial activation in postmortem Parkinson’s disease brains as a feature of brain neuroinflammation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] Brochard and colleagues report brain infiltration by CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, but not B cells, in postmortem human Parkinson disease specimens and in the MPTP mouse model during neuronal degeneration. (low confidence) — https://www.jci.org/articles/view/36470 · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] Sulzer and colleagues report that α-synuclein-derived peptides act as antigenic epitopes driving helper and cytotoxic T cell responses in patients with Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/nature22815 · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Within the MPTP mouse model, Brochard and colleagues attribute T cell-mediated dopaminergic toxicity predominantly to CD4+ T cells requiring FasL expression rather than IFNγ. (low confidence) — https://www.jci.org/articles/view/36470 · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Mazzulli and colleagues report that functional loss of glucocerebrosidase compromises lysosomal protein degradation in primary cultures or human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3132082/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] The Mouton-Liger review describes mammalian-cell evidence that PINK1 and Parkin jointly regulate clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria through autophagy and lysosomal degradation, termed mitophagy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation
- [statement] McWilliams and colleagues report that loss of Pink1 did not alter basal mitophagy in the mouse tissues examined apart from pancreatic islets; this limits extrapolation from depolarization-induced pathway activation to basal mitochondrial turnover. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5807059/ · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/
- [statement] Brochard and colleagues report attenuation of MPTP-induced dopaminergic cell death in mice lacking CD4. (low confidence) — https://www.jci.org/articles/view/36470 · keywords: Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation

## Research summary — Neurodegeneration mechanisms: proteostasis, mitochondria and neuroinflammation

Research connects impaired protein degradation, mitochondrial quality control and inflammatory responses in Parkinson’s disease. Patient-derived neuronal studies link dopamine oxidation to mitochondrial and lysosomal dysfunction. Mouse experiments distinguish basal mitochondrial turnover from stress-induced mitophagy and probe immune contributions to neuronal death. Human immune observations and model findings have different causal scope; pathway activation alone does not establish completed mitochondrial clearance.
